holidays.name: Vanilla Ice Cream Day
holidays.description: Vanilla gets a day of its own. It's the classic scoop that people call plain, even though it's the base for almost every sundae, float, and pie à la mode. Today is a good day to give the humble white scoop some credit, ideally with a cone and a little sprinkle drama.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance that falls in the middle of National Ice Cream Month in July. It is one of several flavor-themed days in the ice cream calendar.
holidays.funFact: Real vanilla comes from orchid pods, and each flower must be pollinated by hand outside its native Mexico. That labor makes vanilla one of the world's priciest spices, and the 'plain' flavor is a lot less plain than it sounds.

holidays.name: Gorgeous Grandma Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate grandmothers who are stylish, sassy, and full of life. It's a good excuse to tell Grandma she looks fabulous, or to take her out for a fancy lunch.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It encourages people to appreciate and pamper the grandmas in their lives.
holidays.funFact: Grandmothers get several days of recognition around the world. This one is a lighthearted, glamour-focused addition to National Grandparents Day, which is held in September in the U.S.

holidays.name: Hot Enough For Ya Day
holidays.description: This day honors the most overused small talk of midsummer. Strangers, coworkers, and neighbors all ask the same sweaty question during a heat wave, and today you're encouraged to ask it, answer it, and groan about it.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance that falls in the hottest stretch of summer, the Dog Days. It pokes fun at the familiar greeting people use during sweltering weather.
holidays.funFact: Late July is statistically one of the hottest times of year across much of the Northern Hemisphere. That makes today a good date for this day, and a good time to be near an ice cream cone.
